question: If sin 2x = cos 60° cos 30° + sin 60° sin 30°, then which of the following is a possible value of tan x + sec x? (0 < x < 90°)
solution:
Given:

sin 2x = cos 60° cos 30° + sin 60° sin 30°

Concept used:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dc116d26b92d04e13dc77acded25f436fa82e69fd412bed9c969ed5d9be8905b.png] 

Calculation:

sin2x = cos60°cos30° + sin60°sin30°

⇒ sin2x = (1/2 × √3/2) + (√3/2 × 1/2)

⇒ sin2x = √3/4 + √3/4

⇒ sin2x = 2√3/4

⇒ sin2x = √3/2

⇒ sin2x = sin60° 

⇒ 2x = 60°

⇒ x = 30°

Now,

tanx + secx

⇒ tan30° + sec30°

⇒ 1/√3 + 2/√3

⇒ (1 + 2)/√3

⇒ 3/√3

⇒ √3

**∴ The value of tanx + secx is sqrt 3 .**
